analysis:
Examined the test file DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift. Unit :4 is the base side, lines 779-1116, and unit :5 is the head side, lines 1-392. The head changes fall at lines 772-834 per the range map. Those lines are outside the supplied head excerpt, so only the base text and the patch excerpt show them.

The patch changes test expectations around ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.discoveryMode. A new `declared` parameter lets a coordinator-served cluster under `auto` ask for Qwen's speculative assistant when the build declares the assistant public for the artifact. Previously, `auto` never asked when the cluster was served through the coordinator.

The base test onlyAPlanWithoutTheAssistantSaysItIsQualifiedForPublicTraffic (base lines 935-970) shows a related rule. A setup with tensorAssistant is labelled not offered for public traffic. The comment there says a setup saved for coordinator pairing carries no assistant, enforced by ClusterConfiguration.validate.

The new declared-path behaviour may relax that coordinator-serving constraint. That bears on the TB-011, T-054 and T-056 qualification and public-model contracts, and on T-007, the serving of outputs from an unqualified configuration.

This is test code only. The production sources (discoveryMode, ClusterPublicModels.declared, ClusterConfiguration.validate, ClusterPairOwnerServing) were not supplied. No regression is evidenced from test changes alone. Coordinator-side qualification and policy remain platform-owned.

Questions for integration:
- Does the production change to discoveryMode and ClusterConfiguration.validate still prevent an assistant-carrying setup from being offered for public coordinator traffic unless it is qualified?
- Is `declared` derived from a build-embedded, verified artifact digest rather than from operator- or environment-controlled input?

The head lines 1-392 are unchanged fixtures: temp homes created 0o700 and the served-speed file set to 0o600. They raise no security concern.
